summary: Sync Reserving Class with ResQ now writes accepted rows one at a time in ArcRho's dependency order instead of alphabetically, so a dataset or method is never saved to ResQ before the datasets it reads.
details: Within one direction, a calculated dataset follows its formula inputs, a DFM follows its input triangle, a BF or Cape Cod method follows the DFM output and priors it links, and a Result Selection follows every source it loads; rows with no link between them keep the review order.

A method whose linked dataset is created earlier in the same run is no longer blocked before writing; the strict check still runs right before each row, so a failed input still stops the rows that read it.
A calculated ArcRho dataset that ResQ does not hold yet is created in ResQ with its formula and left for ResQ to compute, instead of being created and then reported as a failed value write.
The change lives in the Bridge's synchronization session; the macro itself is unchanged and the Bridge must be redeployed to pick it up.
